source_sequence_note: The selected product links the unnumbered AA-207276-4 assembly diagram: four screws 115980, screw then leg, and protected working surface. Eleven assistant-authored actions expand the repeated connection. Corner numbering is assistant-authored. Product-page information supplies load limits and, where linked, care instructions.

components.name: Tabletop
components.description: Square black-brown tabletop. The overall table is 550 × 550 mm; use its existing attachment points.

components.name: Legs
components.description: Four legs, attached by turning each onto an exposed double-ended screw. Schematic proportions are illustrative.

components.name: Double-ended screws
components.description: The official hardware callout identifies four screws numbered 115980. The diagram shows threads at both ends.

steps.title: Prepare a protected surface
steps.instruction: Read the safety information before starting. The assembly diagram shows a soft covering under the tabletop to protect its finish. Place the tabletop with its attachment points accessible, as shown in the assembly diagram.

help.question: Why protect the tabletop?
help.answer: The assembly diagram contrasts a protected surface with damage on an unprotected surface. Use the original diagram to check how the tabletop is supported.

steps.title: Identify the four screws
steps.instruction: Find the four double-ended screws marked 115980 in the official diagram. Match the hardware before proceeding. Keep the tabletop and four legs ready.

help.question: Which screw is this?
help.answer: Look for the double-ended threaded fastener illustrated beside “4×” and “115980” on the official page.

help.question: What if the hardware does not match?
help.answer: Stop and compare your product and hardware with the official document. This tutorial supports only the selected LACK variant; do not substitute an unverified screw.

steps.title: Insert the screws into the tabletop
steps.instruction: The first close-up shows a double-ended screw being turned by hand into a tabletop attachment point, leaving the other end available for the leg. Follow that diagram for each attachment. The sheet supplies four screws.

help.question: How far should I turn the screw?
help.answer: The booklet does not specify a turn count, torque or insertion depth. Follow the original close-up; this schematic does not supply those missing measurements.

help.question: Why is part of the screw exposed?
help.answer: The next close-up shows the leg attached to the exposed end. The diagram, not the schematic thread shape, is the source for that connection.

steps.title: Turn each leg onto its screw
steps.instruction: The second close-up shows the leg turning onto the exposed screw. Repeat the illustrated connection for the four legs. Keep the tabletop supported on the protective surface shown in the guide.

help.question: Should the leg be pushed straight down?
help.answer: The curved arrows show a turning action. The 3D view highlights the connection; it does not prescribe a turn count or torque.

help.question: What if a leg will not attach?
help.answer: Stop instead of forcing it. Recheck the selected product, fastener identity and orientation against the official close-ups. The assistant cannot diagnose damaged hardware or verify a connection physically.

steps.title: Check the fastenings and care for your table
steps.instruction: Check that the assembly fastenings are properly tightened. The official care sheet says to check them regularly and retighten when necessary. Wipe with a damp cloth, then dry with a clean cloth. Keep the safety limits in mind when using the table.

help.question: How do I clean the table?
help.answer: The care sheet specifies a damp cloth followed by a clean dry cloth.

help.question: Does completing this tutorial certify my assembly?
help.answer: No. Completion records your progress only. An agent-reviewed diagram and an instructional schematic cannot verify the actual fastenings or physical assembly.
